messages:
Ravi P: FYI I ran an onboarding sweep for Asterion-14B int6 on the staging fleet tonight. Short take: int6 gives solid cost wins and latency, but we found a reproducible priming fidelity regression on conversational history-heavy requests (not catastrophic, but visible). Quick notes below.

Elena M: numbers?

Ravi P: Micro-scorecard (convo-priming slice, n=800):
- fp16 baseline: EM 70.4, ROUGE-L 61.3, p50 latency 220ms, token cost ~$0.028 per 1k
- int6 (OPA kernels): EM 67.9, ROUGE-L 59.7, p50 latency 170ms, token cost ~$0.016 per 1k
- int4 (experimental): EM 59.0, ROUGE-L 52.2, p50 latency 140ms, token cost ~$0.009 per 1k
Observed EM delta int6 vs fp16: -2.5 pts (95% CI [-3.8, -1.2]).

Sam K: Int6 looks pretty reasonable. Where do failures cluster?

Ravi P: Failure triage: 1) ordering of multi-step instructions occasionally shuffled for long histories (>600 tokens); 2) numeric precision errors in small tables; 3) slightly higher stop-token misses. Most pronounced when priming contains many bullet lists or numbered steps.

Jia L: Any perf/profiling hints?

Ravi P: Kernel traces show slightly higher accumulator quantization noise on middle layers (layers 12-18) and a small increase in attention-weight variance for positions < -600 (i.e., early tokens). KV cache eviction rates are fine. Suspect quantized softmax instabilities for long prefixes.

Elena M: How much real traffic is this slice?

Sam K: Sampling from last 48h: ~9% of requests have >600 token history; of those, ~3% are flagged as high-importance (editor autosave, GTN live-edit).

Elena M: So full switch to int6 would cut token spend by ~1.75x vs fp16, and int4 ~3x, but int4 regression is large. What's the product impact estimate?

Ravi P: Weighted product quality impact if 100% moved to int6: ~-0.2% net Q metric (small but measurable). If 100% int4: ~-1.6% net. Hybrid routing (short <400 tokens -> int6/int4, long-critical -> fp16) gives about 1.5x spend reduction with <0.1% Q hit.

Sam K: Proposed rollout: start with int6 for non-critical routes and keep fp16 for thin-editor flows.

Elena M: Agree. Can we try model-mixing: int6 for candidates + fp16 rerank? Might recover ordering problems. Any cost math for that?

Ravi P: Quick back-of-envelope: costs per 1k tokens: fp16= $0.028, int6= $0.016. If we do int6 candidate + fp16 rerank (2-pass), token cost roughly = candidate_generation_tokens * $0.016 + rerank_tokens * $0.028. For typical flows where generation_tokens >> rerank_tokens (e.g., 80% gen, 20% rerank) net is ~1.1x fp16 cost — not a win unless we can reduce rerank tokens. So not ideal unless rerank can be cheap (small context) or used selectively.

Jia L: Ops constraints? Canary plan? Metrics for rollback?

Sam K: Canary proposal:
- Target: 3% global traffic for 72h, split by route (search/editor/chat)
- Monitoring: priming EM, top-1 accuracy on GTN slices, latency p95, error budget burn rate, downstream user-facing error increase
- Rollback triggers: priming EM drop >= 3 pts sustained for 20m OR any SIGHIGH incident in that window OR p95 latency increase > 30%

Elena M: Also add automated weekly eval on the priming harness and a daily sampled mini-run; alert if EM delta > 2 pts.

Ravi P: I'll add the priming harness to gs://redwood-evals/asterion/priming/2026-03-19 and wire it to the canary dashboard.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled: asterion-int6-canary -> 2026-03-21T03:00Z (notified #eng-deploy).

Sam K: Routing: please implement route-level preferences: /editor/* -> force fp16; /search/*, /assistant/low-risk -> prefer int6. Also add a safety label for GTN production keys to always map to baseline.

Ravi P: Will create routing policy and a /gt/ label. Also exploring small mitigation: layerwise mixed precision (keep first 6 layers fp16, rest int6) — early microbench shows EM delta reduces to ~-1.0 pt while still achieving ~1.35x cost reduction vs full fp16. More testing needed.

Elena M: That mixed-precision approach sounds promising. If it stabilizes priming we could broaden rollout. Add it as an A/B arm in canary.

Ravi P: Will add 3 arms: fp16 baseline, full int6, and mixed-precision int6. Plan: 3% split evenly => 1% per arm.

Jia L: Final asks for docs: short blurb for product + config snippet for routing and canary flags. Example routing JSON inline so SRE can apply.

Ravi P: Draft routing snippet:
```
{
  "route": "/editor/*",
  "preferred_model": "asterion-14b-fp16",
  "safety_label": "gt-prod"
}
{
  "route": "/assistant/*",
  "preferred_models": ["asterion-14b-int6-mixed","asterion-14b-int6","asterion-14b-fp16"],
  "policy": "prefer-cost-latency"
}
```

I'll post a short rollout note in the GTN handoff doc and attach the eval links.

Sam K: Thank you — pragmatic and low-risk. Once mixed-precision numbers land we can decide wider rollout. :+1:

Ravi P: Upload done: https://storage.redwood.ai/evals/asterion/priming/2026-03-19 (scorecards, logs, sample-failures). Will follow up with mixed-precision microbench results by EOD tomorrow.
